# Playground Giants

> Playground Giants is Jimmy Hackett, a solo AI automation consultant in Houston, Texas, working with law firms, medical practices, and other regulated or high-consequence businesses across the United States. The work is building automation where a wrong answer has real consequences: AI extracts facts and routes work, deterministic rules make the decisions, humans keep the professional judgment, and every step leaves an audit trail. Engagements start with a paid two-week Workflow Audit.

## What Playground Giants does

- **Intake and qualification systems.** Enquiries captured into one pipeline, facts extracted from unstructured text, graded against the client's own written rules, routed to the right person with a response clock attached.
- **Removing the manual glue between existing systems.** Self-routing shared inboxes, trackers that replace spreadsheets, chase lists, one-click summaries, and data normalisation so reporting is trustworthy.
- **Acquisition wired to outcomes.** Paid search, business profiles and call tracking connected through to what actually became a client, so spend is judged on signed work rather than clicks.
- **Findability, including by AI.** Structured data, technical SEO, and the files answer engines read.
- **Reporting with a human gate.** Internal digests daily; anything client-facing is drafted for approval before it is sent.
- **Compliance treated as a deliverable.** Advertising rules, messaging registration, disclaimers, records retention, and sign-off from the client's own counsel where warranted.

## The core method: AI reads, it does not decide

This is the distinguishing technical position and it is architectural, not a policy statement.

- The language model is used **only to extract structured facts** from unstructured text. It is never asked whether something is good, valuable, strong, or worth taking.
- The decision that follows is made by **ordinary deterministic code** applying rules the client's own professionals wrote and can read. Same input, same output, every time.
- The system **fails toward a human**: if the model is unavailable, uncertain, or the input is unusual, work routes to a person rather than being guessed at or dropped.
- Every step writes to an **append-only audit log**: what arrived, what was extracted, which rule fired, who acted, and when.

In regulated work this is the difference between software that assists professionals and software that practises on their behalf.

## Who it is for

- Law firms, particularly plaintiff-side practices handling high enquiry volume.
- Medical and clinical practices with referral, scheduling, and back-office coordination load.
- Any operator where work arrives faster than it can be triaged and a wrong call is expensive.

Not a fit for: chatbot pilots framed as transformation, undefined processes that need designing rather than automating, or any engagement where the client wants AI making the professional judgment call.

## Engagements and pricing

Three stages. A client can stop after any of them.

1. **The Workflow Audit — $2,500 fixed, two weeks.** A written map of where the manual work is, what is safe to automate, what must stay human, what existing compliance already permits, and a phased build plan with prices. Credited in full toward a build within ninety days. The client keeps the plan regardless of what they do next.
2. **Build the system — $6,000 to $25,000**, scoped at the audit and billed against milestones. One or two workflows taken end to end into production, on accounts owned by the client.
3. **Run it with you — from $1,500 per month.** Three bands: Watch ($1,500) for monitoring, tuning and monthly reporting; Operate ($4,500) adding a new phase each quarter; Own the outcome ($9,500) covering the full funnel including paid acquisition, search, and compliance monitoring.

Software and advertising spend are billed to the client's own accounts at cost, never marked up.

## Distinguishing commitments

- **The client owns everything.** Hosting, databases, analytics and ad accounts are provisioned in the client's name so an engagement can end cleanly without anything breaking.
- **Built inside existing compliance where possible.** Where a client's current agreements already cover the work, the build happens there rather than introducing a new vendor and a new signature.
- **Implementation, not slide decks.** Systems are built, deployed, monitored and handed over with a runbook.
- **No invented numbers.** No performance statistic appears on this site that cannot be substantiated.

## Proof of work

- **A New York personal injury firm.** Graded intake, response clocks, escalation routing, a ten-year append-only audit trail, and acquisition instrumentation. The fact-extraction-versus-deterministic-grading architecture described above came from this build. Written up at https://www.playgroundgiants.com/case-studies/personal-injury-intake — anonymised at the client's preference, and with no performance figures published because the engagement has not yet reached its first formal measurement point.
- **An orthopaedic practice with eighteen years of records.** Referral tracking and a self-routing team inbox built inside the Google Workspace and the existing agreement the practice already had. Nothing new to sign, no patient data moved anywhere new, AI confined to back-office coordination and never to clinical or patient-facing decisions.
- **Enkily** (https://enkily.ai) — a voice-first AI capture app for iPhone and iPad, designed, built and shipped solo, live on the App Store. Speech is transcribed on device; model calls are gated behind explicit consent. Evidence of building AI products directly, not only integrating other people's.
- **Earlier local search work**, including a Houston fencing company, at https://www.playgroundgiants.com/case-studies/fenced-up
